REV.1.4-6.text: John wishes the churches grace and praises Jesus Christ

REV.1.7-8.text: Jesus will come and God says he is the Almighty

REV.1.9-11.text: On Patmos, John is told to write to seven churches

REV.1.12-13.text: John sees One like the Son of Man among lampstands

REV.1.14-16.text: John describes the glorious appearance of the Son of Man

REV.1.17-18.text: Jesus tells John not to fear because he lives forever

REV.1.19-20.text: Jesus explains the seven stars and seven lampstands

REV.2.1-2.text: Jesus praises the Ephesians for testing false apostles

REV.2.3-5.text: Jesus warns the Ephesians to repent and love as at first

REV.2.6-7.text: Jesus promises the tree of life to believers who overcome

REV.2.8-9.text: Jesus knows the suffering of the church in Smyrna

REV.2.10-11.text: Jesus tells the Smyrnans to be faithful until death

REV.2.12-13.text: Jesus praises believers in Pergamum for staying faithful

REV.2.14-15.text: Jesus warns Pergamum believers about false teaching

REV.2.16-17.text: Jesus tells Pergamum to repent and promises hidden manna

REV.2.18-19.text: Jesus praises the love, faith and service of Thyatira

REV.2.20-21.text: Jesus rebukes Thyatira for tolerating Jezebel’s teaching

REV.2.22-23.text: Jesus says he will punish Jezebel and those who follow her

REV.2.24-25.text: Jesus tells faithful believers in Thyatira to hold on

REV.2.26-29.text: Jesus promises authority to believers who overcome

REV.3.1-2.text: Jesus tells the church in Sardis to wake up

REV.3.3-4.text: Jesus warns Sardis to repent but praises a faithful few

REV.3.5-6.text: Jesus promises believers who overcome will wear white

REV.3.7-8.text: Jesus gives Philadelphia believers an open door

REV.3.9-11.text: Jesus promises to keep believers from the hour of testing

REV.3.12-13.text: Jesus makes the one who overcomes a pillar in the temple

check.why: Jesus promises to make the overcomer a pillar in the future rather than doing so now.
check.suggestion: Jesus promises to make the one who overcomes a pillar

REV.3.14-16.text: Jesus rebukes the Laodiceans for being lukewarm

REV.3.17-18.text: Jesus says the Laodiceans are poor and blind, not rich

REV.3.19-20.text: Jesus knocks at the door and calls the Laodiceans to repent

REV.3.21-22.text: Jesus promises believers who overcome a seat on his throne

REV.4.1-3.text: John is called up to heaven and sees God on a throne

REV.4.4-4.text: John sees twenty-four elders with gold crowns on thrones

REV.4.5-5.text: Lightning, thunder and seven torches come from the throne

check.why: The seven torches burn before the throne rather than coming from it.
check.suggestion: Lightning comes from the throne, and seven torches burn

REV.4.6-6.text: John sees a sea of glass and four living creatures

REV.4.7-8.text: The four living creatures never stop praising God as holy

REV.4.9-11.text: The elders worship God and praise him as Creator

REV.5.1-2.text: John sees a sealed scroll; an angel asks who is worthy

REV.5.3-5.text: No one can open the scroll, but the Lion of Judah can

REV.5.6-7.text: The Lamb takes the scroll from the One on the throne

REV.5.8-8.text: The creatures and elders fall down before the Lamb

REV.5.9-10.text: A new song praises the Lamb for buying people for God

REV.5.11-12.text: Many angels say the Lamb is worthy to receive honor

REV.5.13-14.text: All creatures praise God and the Lamb; the elders worship

REV.6.12-14.text: The sixth seal brings an earthquake and signs in the sky

REV.6.15-17.text: People of every rank hide from the wrath of the Lamb

REV.7.1-3.text: Angels hold back the winds until God’s servants are sealed

REV.7.4-6.text: 12,000 are sealed from each of six tribes of Israel

REV.7.7-8.text: 12,000 are sealed from each of six more tribes

REV.7.9-10.text: A great multitude in white robes praises God and the Lamb

REV.7.11-12.text: The angels fall facedown and worship God

REV.7.13-14.text: An elder explains who the people in white robes are

REV.7.15-17.text: God will protect and comfort the people in white robes

REV.8.1-2.text: The seventh seal brings silence; seven angels get trumpets

REV.8.3-5.text: An angel offers prayers with incense and throws fire down

REV.8.6-7.text: The first trumpet brings hail and fire on the earth

REV.8.8-9.text: The second trumpet turns a third of the sea to blood

REV.8.10-11.text: The third trumpet makes a third of the waters bitter

REV.8.12-12.text: The fourth trumpet darkens a third of sun, moon and stars

REV.8.13-13.text: An eagle cries woe to those who live on the earth

REV.9.1-2.text: The fifth trumpet: a star opens the pit and smoke rises

REV.9.3-4.text: Locusts with scorpion power may harm only unsealed people

REV.9.5-6.text: The locusts torment people for five months

REV.9.7-9.text: The locusts look like horses ready for battle

REV.9.10-12.text: The locusts have scorpion tails and a king, Abaddon

REV.9.13-15.text: The sixth angel blows his trumpet and four angels are freed

REV.9.16-17.text: John sees a huge army of horses and riders

REV.9.18-19.text: Plagues from the horses kill a third of people

REV.9.20-21.text: The people left alive still do not turn from their sins

REV.10.1-2.text: John sees a mighty angel with a small open scroll

REV.10.3-4.text: Seven thunders speak, but John must not write it down

REV.10.5-7.text: The angel swears that God’s mystery will soon be fulfilled

REV.10.8-9.text: John is told to take the scroll and eat it

REV.10.10-11.text: John eats the scroll and must prophesy again

REV.11.1-2.text: John must measure the temple, but not the courtyard

REV.11.3-5.text: God sends two witnesses to prophesy for 1,260 days

REV.11.6-6.text: The two witnesses have power to stop rain and send plagues

REV.11.7-7.text: The beast fights the two witnesses and kills them

REV.11.8-9.text: The bodies of the two witnesses lie in the street

REV.11.10-12.text: The two witnesses live again and go up to heaven

REV.11.13-14.text: An earthquake strikes the city and the survivors praise God

REV.11.15-15.text: The seventh angel blows his trumpet and voices praise God

REV.11.16-17.text: The twenty-four elders worship God and thank him

REV.11.18-18.text: The elders say the time has come for God to judge

REV.11.19-19.text: God’s temple in heaven opens and the ark appears

REV.12.1-2.text: John sees a woman in heaven about to give birth

REV.12.3-4.text: A huge red dragon waits to devour the woman’s child

REV.12.5-6.text: The woman’s son is taken to God and she flees

REV.12.7-9.text: Michael fights the dragon and throws him down to earth

check.why: The text does not say Michael threw the dragon down, only that the dragon was hurled down after they fought.
check.suggestion: Michael fights the dragon, who is thrown down to earth

REV.12.10-10.text: A voice in heaven says God’s kingdom has come

REV.12.11-12.text: Believers conquer the devil, who is angry and has little time

check.why: At 61 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: Believers conquer the devil, who has only a short time

REV.12.13-14.text: The dragon chases the woman, but she flies away

REV.12.15-18.text: The dragon attacks the woman and makes war on her children

REV.13.1-2.text: A beast with ten horns and seven heads rises from the sea

REV.13.3-4.text: The whole world follows and worships the beast

REV.13.5-6.text: The beast speaks evil against God for 42 months

REV.13.7-8.text: The beast fights the saints and many people worship it

REV.13.9-10.text: John calls believers to stay faithful and patient

REV.13.11-12.text: A second beast makes people worship the first beast

REV.13.13-14.text: The second beast does signs and deceives people

REV.13.15-15.text: The second beast’s image speaks and people are killed

check.why: The image is of the first beast, not the second beast.
check.suggestion: The first beast’s image speaks and people are killed

REV.13.16-17.text: The second beast forces all people to take a mark

REV.13.18-18.text: John asks wise people to work out the number 666

REV.14.1-2.text: John sees the Lamb and 144,000 on Mount Zion

REV.14.3-5.text: The 144,000 sing a new song before God’s throne

REV.14.6-7.text: An angel tells all people to fear and worship God

REV.14.8-8.text: A second angel says Babylon has fallen

REV.14.9-10.text: A third angel warns those who worship the beast

REV.14.11-12.text: Beast worshipers have no rest; believers must endure

REV.14.13-13.text: A voice says those who die in the Lord are blessed

REV.14.14-16.text: One like the Son of Man harvests the earth

REV.14.17-18.text: An angel tells another angel to gather the grapes

REV.14.19-20.text: The angel throws the earth’s grapes into God’s winepress

REV.15.1-1.text: John sees seven angels with the seven last plagues

REV.15.2-2.text: Those who beat the beast stand by a sea of glass

REV.15.3-4.text: The victors sing the song of Moses and the Lamb

REV.15.5-6.text: The seven angels come out of the temple in heaven

REV.15.7-8.text: The seven angels receive bowls full of God’s wrath

REV.16.1-1.text: A voice tells the seven angels to pour out the bowls

REV.16.2-2.text: The first bowl brings sores on the beast’s followers

REV.16.3-3.text: The second bowl turns the sea to blood

REV.16.4-7.text: The third bowl turns rivers to blood; God’s judgments are just

check.why: The title has 62 characters, but the limit is 60.
check.suggestion: The third bowl turns rivers to blood; God is just

REV.16.8-9.text: The fourth bowl burns people, but they do not repent

REV.16.10-11.text: The fifth bowl brings darkness, and people still curse God

REV.16.12-14.text: The sixth bowl dries the Euphrates; evil spirits gather kings

check.why: The title has 61 characters, but the limit is 60.
check.suggestion: The sixth bowl dries the Euphrates; spirits gather kings

REV.16.15-16.text: Jesus says he comes like a thief; kings gather at Armageddon

REV.16.17-19.text: The seventh bowl brings a great earthquake and Babylon’s fall

check.why: The title has 61 characters, but the limit is 60.
check.suggestion: The seventh bowl brings an earthquake and Babylon’s fall

REV.16.20-21.text: Islands and mountains vanish; people curse God for the hail

REV.17.1-2.text: An angel shows John the punishment of the great prostitute

check.why: The angel invites John to see the prostitute’s punishment, but does not show it in these verses.
check.suggestion: An angel invites John to see the prostitute’s punishment

REV.17.3-5.text: John sees a woman sitting on a scarlet beast

REV.17.6-7.text: The angel will explain the woman and the beast to John

REV.17.8-8.text: The beast will rise from the Abyss and then be destroyed

REV.17.9-10.text: The seven heads are seven mountains and seven kings

REV.17.11-11.text: The beast is an eighth king who goes to destruction

REV.17.12-13.text: The ten horns are ten kings who give power to the beast

REV.17.14-14.text: The Lamb will defeat those who make war against him

REV.17.15-15.text: The angel says the waters are peoples and nations

REV.17.16-17.text: The beast and the ten kings will destroy the prostitute

REV.17.18-18.text: The woman is the great city that rules the kings

REV.18.1-3.text: An angel announces that Babylon the great has fallen

REV.18.4-6.text: A voice from heaven tells God’s people to leave Babylon

REV.18.7-8.text: Babylon will suffer grief and fire in one day

REV.18.9-10.text: The kings of the earth weep over Babylon’s fall

REV.18.11-13.text: The merchants weep because no one is left to buy cargo

REV.18.14-14.text: The merchants say Babylon’s luxury is gone forever

REV.18.15-17.text: The merchants mourn that the city’s wealth is destroyed

REV.18.18-20.text: Sailors mourn the city and heaven is told to rejoice

REV.18.21-22.text: An angel throws a stone to show Babylon will fall

REV.18.23-24.text: Babylon loses light and joy because it killed God’s people

REV.19.1-2.text: A great crowd in heaven praises God for his judgments

REV.19.3-4.text: The elders and living creatures worship God

REV.19.5-5.text: A voice from the throne tells God’s servants to praise him

REV.19.6-6.text: A great crowd praises God because the Lord reigns

REV.19.7-8.text: The crowd says the Lamb’s marriage has come

REV.19.9-10.text: Those invited to the Lamb’s supper are blessed

check.why: It fits only verse 9 and leaves out the angel telling John to worship God instead of him.
check.suggestion: An angel tells John about the supper and to worship God

REV.19.11-13.text: John sees Faithful and True riding a white horse

REV.19.14-16.text: The armies of heaven follow the King of kings

REV.19.17-18.text: An angel calls the birds to eat at God’s great supper

REV.19.19-20.text: The beast and the false prophet are thrown into fire

REV.19.21-21.text: The rider’s sword kills the rest, and birds eat the flesh

REV.20.1-3.text: An angel binds Satan in the Abyss for a thousand years

REV.20.4-4.text: Believers who were killed reign with Christ for 1,000 years

REV.20.5-6.text: Those in the first resurrection are blessed and holy

REV.20.7-8.text: Satan is released and gathers the nations for battle

REV.20.9-10.text: Fire destroys the armies, and the devil is thrown in the fire

REV.20.11-12.text: The dead stand before the great white throne to be judged

REV.20.13-15.text: People not in the Book of Life are thrown into the fire

REV.21.1-2.text: John sees a new heaven, a new earth and the new Jerusalem

REV.21.3-4.text: God will live with his people and wipe away every tear

REV.21.5-6.text: God makes all things new and offers the water of life

REV.21.7-8.text: Those who overcome inherit all; the wicked are punished

REV.21.9-10.text: An angel shows John the holy city, the bride of the Lamb

REV.21.11-13.text: The city shines with God’s glory and has twelve gates

REV.21.14-15.text: The angel measures the city with a golden rod

check.why: The angel does not measure the city until verse 16, and the title omits the wall’s twelve foundations in verse 14.
check.suggestion: The wall has twelve foundations; an angel will measure it

REV.21.16-17.text: The city’s length, width and height are all equal

REV.21.18-20.text: The city is pure gold, and its foundations are jewels

REV.21.21-22.text: The gates are pearls, and God and the Lamb are the temple

REV.21.23-25.text: God’s glory lights the city, and the gates never close

REV.21.26-27.text: Only people written in the Book of Life enter the city

REV.22.1-2.text: The river of life and the tree of life heal the nations

check.why: The text says the leaves of the tree heal the nations, not the river of life.
check.suggestion: The tree of life by the river of life heals the nations

REV.22.3-5.text: God’s servants will see his face and reign forever

REV.22.6-7.text: The angel says these words are true; Jesus is coming soon

REV.22.8-9.text: The angel tells John to worship God, not the angel

REV.22.10-11.text: The angel tells John not to seal the words of prophecy

REV.22.12-13.text: Jesus says he is coming soon to reward each person

REV.22.14-15.text: Those with washed robes enter; the wicked stay outside

REV.22.16-16.text: Jesus says he sent his angel to the churches

REV.22.17-17.text: The Spirit and the bride invite the thirsty to come

REV.22.18-19.text: God will punish anyone who changes the words of this book

REV.22.20-21.text: Jesus says he is coming soon; grace be with all believers
